predecessors.name: Russian Empire
predecessors.text: the Russian governorates of Courland, Livonia and Vitebsk's Latgale, taken from the empire in 1918

ledger.x: 1918: Latvia declares independence at Riga on 18 November 1918 (infobox 'Declared: 18 November 1918') after breaking away from the Russian Empire.

1918: the Red Army invades on 1 December 1918; the Latvian Socialist Soviet Republic is formed in Russia on 17 December and proclaimed on 13 January 1919; Riga falls to the Red Army on 3 January 1919.
1919: the West Russian Volunteer Army (Bermontians) attacks Riga on 8 October 1919; Latvian forces retake Riga on 11 November.
1919: by early December 1919 the Bermontian force had been pushed out of Latvia.
1920: the Latvian-Soviet Riga Peace Treaty is signed on 11 August 1920, ending the war (talks began 16 April 1920).
1940: ultimatums on 16 June, Soviet troops enter Latvia on 17 June 1940 and a pro-Soviet government is installed on 20 June.
1940: occupation ends in annexation: on 5 August 1940 the USSR grants the rigged Saeima's petition of 21 July and Latvia becomes 'the 15th Soviet republic'.

1940: the Soviet Union incorporates Latvia on 5 August 1940 as the Latvian SSR; the Latvian government, the ECHR, the US and the EU hold the occupation and incorporation illegal (1996 parliamentary declaration: 'a military occupation and an illegal incorporation'); Russia says it was legal.
1991: after the declaration of 4 May 1990 Latvia 'restored full independence on 21 August 1991, in the aftermath of the failed Soviet coup attempt'.

wars.name: Latvian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Latvia cleared the Red Army, the Landeswehr and the Bermontians and signed the Riga Peace Treaty with Soviet Russia on 11 August 1920.

wars.name: Soviet occupation of Latvia (1940)
wars.outcome: No fighting: ultimatum 16 June, entry 17 June, incorporation 5 August 1940.

wars.name: Reoccupation of Latvia (1944-1945)
wars.outcome: Soviets retake Riga on 13 October 1944; the Courland Pocket holds until 10 May 1945.
